title: Rider NEM-R and Rider NEM-A — Phase-In of the Non-Bypassable Charge on Revalued Export Credits (Net Energy Metering)
content:
Under the Net Energy Metering riders whose basis is the retail energy rate less the non-bypassable charge — Rider NEM-R Residential Net Energy Metering and Rider NEM-A Aggregated Net Energy Metering, each with a non-bypassable charge of 0.02215 USD per kWh — the charge deducted from a revalued export rate is phased in over the agreement's first months of operation.

**Rule.** Under the retail-rate-less-non-bypassable-charge basis, when the whole calendar months from the permission to operate date to the export credit's billing period end are at least the full-charge month count of 24, the rider's non-bypassable charge is deducted in full. Under that basis, when those months are fewer than 24, the rider's non-bypassable charge multiplied by the phase-in share of 0.50, rounded to five decimals, is deducted. Otherwise nothing is deducted.

The deduction applies to both revalued rates. The permission to operate date is the date recorded on the agreement; the billing period end is that of the export credit revalued.

## Deduction by months in operation

| Rider basis | Whole calendar months from permission to operate to the billing period end | Non-bypassable charge deducted |
|---|---|---|
| Retail energy rate less the non-bypassable charge | 24 or more | 0.02215, in full |
| Retail energy rate less the non-bypassable charge | Fewer than 24 | 0.02215 multiplied by 0.50 is 0.011075, rounded to 0.01108 |
| Retail energy rate (Rider NEM-L Legacy Net Energy Metering) | Any | Nothing |

## Boundary cases (hypothetical)

- Permission to operate on 10 March of one year; export credit for a billing period ending 9 March two years later: 23 whole months, so 0.01108 is deducted.
- The same agreement, billing period ending 10 March two years later: 24 whole months, so 0.02215 is deducted in full.
